questions.text: How should the thermostat be powered, given how fast a command from your phone must take effect? With WiFi, batteries only last a year if the device sleeps and checks for commands now and then. (The heating schedule and the room control work offline in every option.)
options: Recommended: powered from the wall (needs the neutral wire in the box, live is already there because the relays switch 230 V). Phone commands act in about 1 second, no batteries ever. Adds about 2-3 USD.
One AA battery, about 1 year. Phone commands act within about 1 hour (the device checks once per hour, or at once if you press its button).
Two AA batteries, about 1 year. Phone commands act within about 20-30 minutes. Needs the whole wall box or a deeper two-board build (+1-2 USD).
Two AAA batteries, about 1 year. Phone commands act within about 1 hour; same life as one AA but a larger holder. (One AAA alone would give a check only every 4-5 hours, so it is not offered.)
questions.why: Conflict C1/C4 in conflicts.md: 1 x AA leaves about 153 uW for WiFi = about 26 wake-ups/day at 0.5 J each; a 15-minute check needs 8 Wh/yr (3 x AA); an always-connected radio needs about 68 Wh/yr, which only mains can provide.

questions.text: How should it sit in the Italian 503 wall box?
options: Recommended: as a standard 3-module device that clips into the normal support frame behind any brand's 3-module plate (front 67.5 x 45 mm, about 38 mm deep). Fits with one AA or mains power.
Fill the whole 503 box behind a blank cover plate (about 90 x 55 mm board). Room for any battery choice, but no other socket or switch can share that box, and the cover may need to be custom.
As a 2-module device next to a switch or socket in the same box. Only possible without batteries (mains-powered), and very tight.
questions.why: Conflict C3: the 230 V parts need 6 mm safety gaps; in a 3-module board (2730 mm2) the relay zone uses 960-1350 mm2, leaving room for one AA (912 mm2) only with compact relays.

questions.text: What will the two outputs switch, per room?
options: Recommended: 230 V thermoelectric valve heads on radiators/manifold (up to about 4 heads per room) or a zone valve / boiler enable contact. We rate each output 5 A at 230 V, voltage-free contact (installer wires live to it). Small relays, fits the 3-module size.
Larger loads such as an electric heater or a pump directly (up to 16 A each). Bigger relays: no room for an AA battery in the 3-module size.
I don't know yet: design for 5 A and state in the manual that larger loads need an external contactor.
questions.why: The load sets the relay size, which decides whether the battery fits (C3). Thermoelectric heads use about 2-3 W each, so 4 heads draw about 55 mA; 5 A leaves a large margin for inrush.

questions.text: If the battery runs out (or power is cut), what should the heating do?
options: Recommended: switch heating OFF before the battery is empty, and send low-battery warnings to the app starting at least 30 days before. No extra cost.
Switch OFF even if someone pulls the battery out suddenly (adds a small energy reserve, about 0.5-1 USD).
Leave the heating as it was (on stays on). No cost, but heating may run uncontrolled until the battery is replaced.
Leave heating ON (frost protection first, accepts wasted energy).
questions.why: Conflict C2: on battery, only latching relays are possible (a normal relay coil would need about 263 Wh per season, the battery has 1.3-6 Wh), and latching relays keep their last state when the battery dies.
